digest.headline: The US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady as technology shares tumbled.

lede.b: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady to fight rising prices, which are when everyday goods cost more over time. The central bank made this choice even as borrowing costs stayed high. Meanwhile, technology shares dropped sharply across Wall Street. Investors pulled their money out of artificial intelligence companies.
lede.i: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady despite persistent inflation and ongoing pressure on borrowing costs. This status quo decision coincided with a sharp sell-off in technology equities. The Nasdaq index dropped by 2.9% as investors rotated capital away from artificial intelligence sectors.
lede.a: The Federal Reserve maintained its target range despite sticky inflation prints, eschewing policy easing. Concurrently, the Nasdaq index retreated 2.9% as market participants de-grossed artificial intelligence exposure during a broad risk-off session.

items.b: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady, and technology shares led a market drop.

thread.b: Central banks made choices about interest rates today. Stock markets in several countries saw falling share prices. Companies reported mixed financial results.

thread.a: Monetary authorities navigated policy decisions against a backdrop of equity market corrections. Technology sector weakness weighed on indices across multiple jurisdictions.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Fed holds rates as tech stocks tumble

stories.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady
stories.b: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady. This is the cost of borrowing money. The central bank made this choice because price increases remain persistent. Price increases are when things cost more over time, which officials call inflation.
stories.i: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady. Policymakers acted in the face of persistent inflation. The central bank held borrowing costs unchanged despite ongoing pressure.
stories.a: The Federal Reserve maintained its target rate unchanged. Policymakers held policy steady against stubborn inflation readings. The decision left the benchmark rate where it was before the meeting.

stories.t: Technology shares lead market drop
stories.b: The Nasdaq index fell by 2.9%. An index is a group of company shares tracked together to see how a market is doing. Wall Street entered a show me phase as tech stocks plunged. Investors moved away from tech and artificial intelligence.
stories.i: The Nasdaq index dropped by 2.9%. Wall Street entered a show me phase as technology shares plunged. Investors shifted capital away from artificial intelligence sectors.
stories.a: The Nasdaq fell by 2.9%. Wall Street entered a show me phase as equities dropped. Investors retreated from technology and artificial intelligence holdings.

politics.b: NBC News published five charts showing the state of the U.S. economy. These charts came out ahead of the midterms. Voters look at economic conditions before casting ballots.
politics.i: NBC News released five charts detailing the U.S. economy. The data arrived ahead of the midterm elections. Economic indicators remain central to the political backdrop.
politics.a: NBC News outlined the state of the U.S. economy through five charts. The release preceded the midterm elections. Macroeconomic metrics frame the political debate.

timeline: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady as tech stocks plunged.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: UK Budget reactions and mortgage lending rules

stories.t: UK Government Budget and British Government Bonds
stories.b: UK government bonds are official loans that investors make to the state in exchange for regular interest payments. The recent state budget followed specific financial rules and maintained fiscal headroom, which represents the safety margin governments keep to handle unexpected costs. British gilts responded positively to these fiscal choices. UK gilts are simply bonds issued specifically by the British government.
stories.i: UK gilts rallied following a government budget that adhered to established fiscal rules. Maintaining fiscal headroom reassured investors regarding public borrowing limits. The recent fiscal announcements shaped near-term sovereign debt pricing across the UK market. British gilts finished the session higher.
stories.a: UK sovereign debt reacted favourably to a fiscal package that respected self-imposed borrowing constraints and preserved fiscal headroom. The maintenance of credible buffers reduced term premia embedded in British gilts. Market participants repriced UK gilts after the fiscal event removed immediate tail risk on debt issuance targets.

stories.t: Bank of England Examines Mortgage Limits
stories.b: The Bank of England functions as the central bank of the nation, acting as the main bank for other banks and setting monetary policy. Officials at the institution are currently exploring ways to ease important limits on riskier mortgage lending. Mortgages are special loans used specifically to buy property. Changing these lending limits affects how easily people can borrow money to buy houses.
stories.i: The Bank of England started exploring potential revisions to key limits on riskier mortgage lending. Central bank officials are reviewing macroprudential guardrails governing property loans. Modifying these structural caps alters the risk profile for residential mortgage portfolios across commercial lenders. The Bank of England oversees the regulatory framework governing these housing finance limits.
stories.a: The Bank of England initiated exploratory work into relaxing macroprudential constraints on higher-risk mortgage lending. Adjusting these structural lending caps reconfigures systemic risk tolerances within the UK housing finance sector. The central bank evaluates transmission channels between capital requirements and residential mortgage availability. The Bank of England maintains supervisory oversight over these specific lending boundaries.

politics.b: The government released a new state budget that followed strict financial rules. Observers noted that the fiscal plans maintained financial headroom. Financial analysts examined the details of the budget to see how citizens might be affected. The recent fiscal package shaped market responses across the UK.
politics.i: The UK government delivered a budget constrained by internal fiscal rules. Fiscal headroom remained a central metric for evaluating the sustainability of public finances. Market participants processed the fiscal announcements and their implications for state borrowing. The latest budget outcomes continue to influence domestic financial conditions.
politics.a: The administration formulated a fiscal framework anchored by predetermined borrowing rules and deficit targets. Preserved fiscal headroom served to anchor investor expectations regarding medium-term debt trajectories. Institutional scrutiny focused on the longer-term macroeconomic assumptions underpinning the budget. The fiscal announcements dictate current sovereign debt dynamics and policy compliance.

timeline: Financial Times reports the Bank of England is exploring easing limits on riskier mortgage lending.
StoneX publishes analysis on UK gilts rewarding the recent Budget.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German inflation cools while stock index slips

stories.t: German Inflation Rate Declines
stories.b: Inflation is when things cost more over time. The rate of price growth in Germany slowed down recently. This is called inflation cooling. Prices are still rising, just at a slower pace.
stories.i: German inflation decelerated over the period. Price pressures in the economy moderated. Consumer costs rose at a gentler trajectory.
stories.a: German headline inflation printed lower on the latest reading. The deceleration reflects easing domestic price momentum across key consumer baskets. Rate path expectations adjusted as the disinflationary print crossed screens.

stories.t: DAX Index Drops Despite Price Data
stories.b: The DAX is a group of big company shares in Germany. A share is a tiny piece of a business that you can buy. The DAX index went down in value today. This happened even though price growth slowed down.
stories.i: The DAX index fell during the session. Equities traded lower despite the softer inflation print. Stock valuations contracted across major sectors.
stories.a: The DAX drifted lower through the trading day. Equity investors shrugged off the benign macroeconomic print. Broad index constituents experienced selling pressure regardless of the easing consumer price data.

politics.b: German economic data releases continue to shape market conditions.
politics.i: German financial markets reacted to updated consumer price metrics.
politics.a: German macroeconomic releases drove localized equity repricing.

timeline: 30 Oct
German inflation figures are published alongside market index updates.
31 Oct
DAX seasonal return charts are updated on financial platforms.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Bank of Japan holds rates while Nikkei and Yen face pressure

stories.t: Bank of Japan Holds Rates
stories.b: The Bank of Japan decided to keep its interest rates steady. This means borrowing costs for money do not go up or down. Japanese Yen futures pared their earlier gains after this announcement.
stories.i: The Bank of Japan held rates steady at its policy meeting. Japanese Yen futures pared gains in response to the central bank decision. Traders adjusted positions following the status quo outcome.
stories.a: The Bank of Japan maintained current policy settings at the latest review. Japanese Yen futures pared gains as the rate hold dashed immediate tightening expectations. Short-term yield differentials against the dollar remained anchored by the decision.

stories.t: Nikkei 225 Encounters AI Wobbles
stories.b: The Nikkei 225 index is a list of big company stocks in Japan. Shares in artificial intelligence dropped recently. This brought the market down to a key support zone, which is a level where prices usually stop falling.
stories.i: The Nikkei 225 index faced selling pressure due to artificial intelligence wobbles. Equities retreated toward a key support zone. Market participants monitored the technical floor closely.
stories.a: The Nikkei 225 drifted lower as artificial intelligence related equities suffered pullbacks. Price action tested a key support zone. Trend followers assessed whether the current technical floor would hold against ongoing sector repricing.

politics.b: Japan held a meeting with a Russian minister. Officials demanded the release of a national who is currently held.
politics.i: Japan officials met with a Russian minister. Tokyo demanded the release of a detained Japanese national during the talks.
politics.a: Japanese representatives engaged a Russian minister in direct talks. Officials formally demanded the release of a detained Japanese national during the diplomatic exchange.

timeline: 30 Oct
Japan met with a Russian minister to demand the release of a detained national.
31 Oct
The Bank of Japan held interest rates steady.

China.label: China
China.sub: Factory activity contracts and corporate earnings vary

stories.t: Chinese Factory Activity Contracts
stories.b: Factory activity in China dropped for the third time in four months. This means manufacturing slowed down across the country. A contraction shows that fewer goods were made than in previous periods. Data from Nikkei Asia confirmed this trend on October 31, 2026.
stories.i: China recorded a manufacturing contraction for the third time in four months. This metric tracks factory output and new orders across industrial sectors. The latest data points to persistent weakness in domestic goods production. Nikkei Asia published the figures on October 31, 2026.
stories.a: China's manufacturing sector registered its third contraction within four months. This print underscores ongoing headwinds in industrial demand and factory gate pricing power. The recurring sub-50 readings indicate persistent structural drag on broader economic momentum. Nikkei Asia reported the data on October 31, 2026.

stories.t: Corporate Earnings and AI Capital Injections
stories.b: TCL Technology grew its nine-month profit by 68% to reach $769m. Kling AI finished a capital increase of 19.8 billion yuan with backing from Kingdee and MetaX. Meanwhile, Changan Automobile reported a loss of 758 million yuan in the third quarter. Guosen Securities saw its third-quarter profit drop by nearly 80% due to trading losses.
stories.i: TCL Technology reported a 68% rise in nine-month profit to $769m. Kling AI closed a 19.8 billion yuan funding round featuring Kingdee and MetaX after Middle Eastern capital exited. Changan Automobile posted a 758 million yuan loss for the third quarter. Guosen Securities suffered an 80% profit plunge as proprietary trading generated a 1.247 billion yuan quarterly loss.
stories.a: TCL Technology posted a 68% year-to-date net income increase to $769m. Kling AI finalized its 19.8 billion yuan equity financing round following late-stage capital reallocation involving Kingdee and MetaX. Changan Automobile swung to a 758 million yuan third-quarter loss while its autonomous driving unit sought fresh funding. Guosen Securities experienced an 80% profit contraction driven by a 1.247 billion yuan loss in proprietary trading desks.

politics.b: Hong Kong residents traveled to Shenzhen to find lower prices. Baidu lowered its search API price to 4.9 yuan per 1,000 calls. China Securities made a net profit of over 10 billion yuan for the first three quarters and put 6 billion Hong Kong dollars into its international business.
politics.i: Cost-conscious visitors from Hong Kong traveled to Shenzhen for cheaper goods and services. Baidu reduced its search API pricing to 4.9 yuan per 1,000 calls. China Securities reported over 10 billion yuan in net profit for the first three quarters and allocated 6 billion Hong Kong dollars to expand international operations.
politics.a: Cross-border consumer flows from Hong Kong to Shenzhen intensified as shoppers sought lower price points. Baidu adjusted its API pricing to 4.9 yuan per 1,000 calls following search model updates. China Securities generated over 10 billion yuan in net profit across the first three quarters while committing 6 billion Hong Kong dollars to international segment expansion.

India.label: India
India.sub: Nifty reclaims 23,000, bank lending rates ease, RBI tightens cyber checks

stories.t: Nifty Reclaims 23,000 as Foreign Investors Return
stories.b: The Nifty stock market index crossed 23,000 points again. Foreign institutional investors became net buyers. This means overseas funds bought more shares than they sold. The Indian rupee ended the session unchanged against the dollar.
stories.i: The Nifty index reclaimed the 23,000 level supported by foreign institutional investors turning net buyers. Equities recovered on Dalal Street over the week. The rupee finished the day unchanged against the dollar.
stories.a: The Nifty benchmark reclaimed 23,000 as foreign portfolio flows turned positive on a weekly basis. Dalal Street staged a recovery following earlier October weakness. The rupee closed flat against the greenback amidst broader equity gains.

stories.t: RBI Reports Decline in Fresh Bank Lending Rates
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India stated that lending rates on fresh bank loans dropped to 8.51% in September. Deposit rates also eased during the same month. Commercial lenders adjusted their pricing as central bank policies took effect.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India reported that lending rates on fresh bank loans declined to 8.51% in September. Deposit rates experienced a corresponding decrease during the month. Financial institutions adjusted yields across retail and corporate books.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India data showed fresh bank loan rates contracting to 8.51% over September. Deposit rates softened concurrently across the banking sector. The transmission of monetary policy continued to compress asset yields for commercial lenders.

stories.t: Central Bank Tightens Cyber Security Regulations for Lenders
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India increased cyber security checks on lenders. This decision followed a series of recent cyber hacks targeting financial institutions. Banks must now meet stricter digital safety standards.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India intensified cyber security audits on lenders following a spate of recent digital hacks. Banking institutions face heightened scrutiny over network vulnerabilities. Regulatory oversight expanded to protect consumer data and core ledgers.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India imposed stricter cyber security protocols on regulated lenders following recent security breaches. Supervisory frameworks targeted digital infrastructure resilience across the banking sector. Institutions face mandatory compliance upgrades to mitigate systemic operational risks.

politics.b: The International Monetary Fund suggested the Indian rupee should act as the primary defense against energy price shocks.
politics.i: The International Monetary Fund framed the rupee as India's initial shock absorber against external energy price volatility.
politics.a: The International Monetary Fund designated the rupee as the primary macro-prudential buffer against imported energy price shocks.

timeline: 30 Sep
Fresh bank lending rates decline to 8.51% according to RBI data
31 Oct
Nifty reclaims the 23,000 threshold as foreign investors turn net buyers

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras finds oil and stocks drop

stories.t: Petrobras makes third Amapá discovery
stories.src: Oil & Gas Middle East · Latin Times · Energy Intelligence
stories.b: Petrobras found a new oil deposit in the Amapá region. This is the third time the company has struck oil there, alongside BP. The discovery happened right before the COP30 climate summit.
stories.i: Petrobras struck its third oil find in the Amapá area with BP. The discovery arrives immediately ahead of the COP30 climate talks, intensifying the debate over energy versus climate policy.
stories.a: Petrobras and BP announced a third hydrocarbon discovery in the Amapá basin. The timing directly precedes the COP30 conference, sharpening domestic and international tension around fossil fuel expansion versus climate commitments.

stories.t: Brazilian stock index records worst week since 2020
stories.b: The Bovespa stock index fell 0.75%. It finished the week at 168,081 points. This marked the worst weekly performance for the index since the pandemic year of 2020.
stories.i: The Bovespa index declined 0.75% to close at 168,081 points. This drop capped the Ibovespa's worst weekly performance since 2020.
stories.a: The Bovespa lost 0.75% to settle at 168,081 points, culminating the Ibovespa's steepest weekly drawdown since the pandemic volatility of 2020.

stories.t: Petrobras refinery operations reach high utilization
stories.b: Petrobras ran its oil refineries at 98% capacity during October. A company director shared this operational update.
stories.i: Petrobras operated its refineries at 98% capacity through October, according to a company director.
stories.a: Refinery utilization at Petrobras averaged 98% in October, as reported by a company director.

politics.b: Brazil faces intense debates over climate policy and oil drilling as global climate summits approach.
politics.i: Discussions surrounding climate policy and fossil fuel exploration intensified ahead of COP30.
politics.a: The juxtaposition of offshore discoveries with international climate conventions accentuates domestic policy friction around hydrocarbon dependency.

timeline: Petrobras reports October refinery utilization at 98% capacity.
Ibovespa records its worst weekly decline since 2020.
Petrobras announces its third oil find in the Amapá region.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco reports production losses and regional supply risks

stories.t: Aramco CEO warns of slow recovery after barrel losses
stories.b: Saudi Aramco is a very large state-owned oil company in Saudi Arabia. The chief executive officer warned that losing 1 billion barrels will slow down the recovery of the oil market. Disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz could push this market recovery into 2027. Two people died after a drone was intercepted near the Shaybah oilfield. Attacks also cut output and flow along the East-West pipeline.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco warned that the loss of 1 billion barrels will delay oil market recovery. Disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz threaten to push recovery into 2027. Separate attacks cut state output and East-West pipeline flows. Two individuals died following a drone interception near the Shaybah oilfield.
stories.a: The chief executive of Saudi Aramco identified the loss of 1 billion barrels as a drag on market recovery timelines. Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions risk deferring sector normalization into 2027. Physical infrastructure attacks simultaneously crimped domestic output and East-West pipeline transmission. A drone interception near the Shaybah oilfield resulted in two fatalities.

stories.t: Saudi Aramco and Sonatrach lift November LPG prices
stories.src: Quantum Commodity Intelligence · EnergyNow.com · Enab Baladi
stories.b: Saudi Aramco and Sonatrach raised official selling prices for liquefied petroleum gas for November. Saudi Arabia also recorded the biggest drop in its Arab Light Asia official selling price in over two decades for August. Syria signed a deal with Saudi Aramco to diversify its fuel supply. Caturus signed a liquefied natural gas supply deal with Saudi Aramco.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco and Sonatrach increased official selling prices for liquefied petroleum gas for November. August saw the largest reduction in Saudi Arabia's Arab Light Asia official selling price in over 20 years. Syria diversified its fuel imports through a new agreement with Saudi Aramco. Caturus finalised a liquefied natural gas supply contract with Saudi Aramco.
stories.a: November liquefied petroleum gas official selling prices were marked higher by Saudi Aramco and Sonatrach. August pricing for Arab Light to Asia sustained its largest downward adjustment in over two decades. Syria established a fuel supply accord with Saudi Aramco to diversify sourcing. Caturus executed a liquefied natural gas supply agreement with the Saudi producer.

politics.b: Saudi Aramco seeks to partner with other countries to expand its oil stockpile. The chief executive stated that energy security beats climate concerns. OPEC sees no peak in oil demand. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates plans to push oil output above 5 million barrels per day next year.
politics.i: Saudi Aramco aims to forge international partnerships to expand its oil stockpile. The chief executive emphasized that energy security supersedes climate considerations. OPEC anticipates no imminent peak in oil demand. Concurrently, the United Arab Emirates targets oil production exceeding 5 million barrels per day next year following its expansion push.
politics.a: Saudi Aramco is pursuing international partnerships to scale its oil stockpile capacity. Leadership affirmed that energy security priorities currently outweigh climate initiatives within institutional frameworks. OPEC projections continue to discount any near-term peak in aggregate oil demand. Concurrently, the United Arab Emirates advances its post-OPEC expansion strategy to lift output above 5 million barrels per day next year.

timeline: Saudi Aramco and Sonatrach raised official selling prices for liquefied petroleum gas for November.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira shifts, cash support begins and road budgets pass

stories.t: Naira Exchange Rates and Political Debates
stories.b: The naira is the money used in Nigeria. Some politicians argue about how strong this money should be compared to the US dollar. One politician says a future leader could make one dollar cost five hundred naira. Other people disagree and say past policies made the currency weak and caused hardship.
stories.i: The naira traded at 1,373 naira per US dollar in the parallel market while foreign reserves slipped. Political figures argued over whether a future administration could strengthen the currency to 500 naira per dollar. Critics blamed previous national leadership and currency inflation policies for deepening hardship.
stories.a: The parallel market rate settled at 1,373 naira per dollar amid declining foreign reserves. Political discourse divided over feasibility projections targeting a 500 naira per dollar valuation, with detractors framing such claims as fallacies rooted in historical macro mismanagement. Debates over currency devaluation continued to spotlight structural hardships from prior administrations.

stories.t: Federal Cash Relief and Infrastructure Spending
stories.b: The federal government started giving fifty thousand naira every month to poor citizens as cash relief. The government also approved six hundred thirty-one billion three million naira to build nine major roads. At the same time, a data rule from the central bank pushed companies to spend billions on local tech infrastructure.
stories.i: The federal government commenced monthly cash disbursements of 50,000 naira to vulnerable citizens. Concurrently, the executive council approved 631.3 billion naira for nine major road projects. Additionally, a central bank data localisation directive spurred multi-billion naira investments in local digital infrastructure.
stories.a: Disbursements of 50,000 naira monthly relief materialized for vulnerable populations alongside a 631.3 billion naira budgetary allocation for nine major arterial roads ratified by the federal executive council. Regulatory pressure from the central bank via data localisation mandates simultaneously catalyzed multi-billion naira capital expenditure in domestic infrastructure.

stories.t: Corporate Financial Results for Nigerian Firms
stories.b: A company named eTranzact International made twenty billion nine hundred ninety million naira in revenue by the end of September. Another firm called Initiates earned three billion seven hundred sixty million naira in revenue during the same quarter. Both companies shared their financial results with the public.
stories.i: eTranzact International reported 20.99 billion naira in revenue from continuing operations for the period ended September 30. Initiates posted 3.76 billion naira in revenue and 1.82 billion naira in profit before tax for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. These corporate earnings reports arrived alongside broader macroeconomic updates on currency valuations.
stories.a: Quarterly disclosures indicated eTranzact International generated 20.99 billion naira in continuing operations revenue through September 30. Initiates concurrently reported 3.76 billion naira in top-line revenue alongside 1.82 billion naira in profit before tax for the quarter ending September 30, 2026. These corporate metrics reflect operating performances published amidst ongoing currency fluctuations.

politics.b: Political groups argued about past economic management and future election promises. One group blamed an old administration for poverty and a weak currency. Another group argued about whether a specific politician could fix the exchange rate if elected.
politics.i: Political campaigns traded accusations over historical governance records concerning poverty, insecurity, and currency depreciation. Debates intensified over campaign pledges regarding future exchange rate targets and macroeconomic management.
politics.a: Partisan factions exchanged criticisms regarding the legacy of past administrations on poverty alleviation and exchange rate stability. Policy debates centered on the credibility of opposition pledges to manipulate currency valuations via political office.

timeline: eTranzact International and Initiates recorded financial periods ending on this date.
The federal government began paying 50,000 naira monthly cash relief to vulnerable citizens.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: ASE Technology shares fall and Vertex Minerals secures approvals

stories.t: ASE Technology Shares Slide Following Market Updates
stories.b: ASE Technology saw its stock fall 11.3%. Shares represent little slices of ownership in a company. Investors look at scores and ratings to decide whether to buy or sell. Wall Street Zen upgraded the stock to Buy. GuruFocus discussed what a GF Score of 75 tells investors.
stories.i: ASE Technology experienced an 11.3% drop in its share price. Wall Street Zen upgraded the stock to Buy. GuruFocus analyzed the investment implications of a GF Score of 75. Market participants parse these signals to adjust portfolio weightings.
stories.a: ASE Technology equities retreated 11.3% as participants digested quantitative inputs and a GF Score of 75. Wall Street Zen revised its stance to Buy. The divergence between the rating upgrade and the sharp equity drawdown highlights conflicting signals in order flow.

stories.t: Vertex Minerals Secures Underground Approvals at Reward
stories.b: Vertex Minerals published its quarterly report. The company secured approvals for extended underground operations at Reward. Mining companies need official permits to dig deeper into the earth. These updates give investors a look at operational progress.
stories.i: Vertex Minerals released its quarterly report detailing regulatory milestones. The firm secured approvals for extended underground operations at Reward. These permissions clear the path for ongoing resource extraction at the site.
stories.a: Vertex Minerals issued its quarterly report confirming regulatory clearance for extended underground operations at Reward. The operational approval removes a key bottleneck for site development. Production schedules now depend on executing the expanded extraction plan.

politics.b: No political news was reported in the sources today.
politics.i: No political developments appeared in the market sources.
politics.a: No macroeconomic policy or political disclosures were present in the source material.

timeline: ASE Technology shares fell 11.3% while the company received a GF Score of 75.
Vertex Minerals reported securing approvals for extended underground operations at Reward.
